subject: How to fill matrix columns from array of vectors?

messages.author: 4a2e6df47f9f0bef
messages.subject: How to fill matrix columns from array of vectors?
parts:
Hello, I want to fill my matrix from array of vectors by appending or assinging them.
(the code is just to show the problem)

matrix[rowsN, factorsCount] allFactors;

from some source data 
vector[rowsN] factors[factorsCount];

ways to do it could be:

for(i in 1:factorsCount)
{
       allFactors[,i] =factors[i] ;
}

or may be I should declare empty matrix and then concatenate it with vectors...

matrix[rowsN, factorsCount] allFactors;
for(i in 1:factorsCount)
{
       allFactors =append_col(allFactors, factors[i]) ;
}

Both approaches give error from the compiler:

"Not a legal assignment, sampling, or function statement.  Note that
  * Assignment statements only allow variables (with optional indexes) on the left;
    if you see an outer function logical_lt (<) with negated (-) second argument,
    it indicates an assignment statement A <- B with illegal left
    side A parsed as expression (A < (-B))."


Which is the correct way to fill matrix from array of vectors?

Regards,
Nikolay

Can you show us a real example. For the toy example you gave, the
right approach would be to declare the variable with the shape you
want to begin with.

And it's "<-" not "=" for assignment in Stan.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to fill matrix columns from array of vectors?
parts:
Although that's not an array of vectors, either, we're
sympathetic to that problem. We need functions that will
start at index N in an array and peel off any given Stan
data type. We have all that in C++ as part of our I/O,
but not exposed as functions in Stan. But it's on our to-do list.

For now, you can use the new slicing functions, though it
looks like there are still some include issues that's blocking
the full functionality there.

- Bob
